newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Swedish debt/currency market closing report.
newsitem.headline: Swedish debt/currency market closing report.

text.p: Swedish long debt yields fell a touch with support from foreign markets and a stronger crown.
"Europe is doing fine and the crown is strengthening. That lent support to the Swedish debt market," one dealer said, adding that sentiment was generally positive in Sweden.
Ten-year bond yields shed three basis points to 6.66 percent. Six-month T-bill rates rose one basis point to 4.13 percent. The crown firmed to 4.4580 against the mark from 4.4720 late on Tuesday.
The main reason is that export companies have bought crowns before closing their books at the end of June, dealers said.

"The most interesting thing about the crown is if it manages to break through the 4.45 level against the mark," one dealer said. "I think it might do that in a couple of weeks. In that case I think we will see trading between 4.40 and 4.50."

The market was now focusing on Swedish May producer prices due on Thursday at 0800 GMT. Producer prices are expected to rise by 0.3 percent on the month, and by 1.1 percent year-on-year according to a Reuter poll.
Swedish May trade surplus was 11.1 billion, lower than expectations, but fail to spark any market reaction.
